Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:35528-Db
Court No. - 10
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 3899 of 2023

Petitioner :- Morimisetty Pandu
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko. And Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Salil Tripathi Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned AGA who appears on behalf of State-respondents and perused the record.

This writ petition has been filed praying the following main reliefs:
"i) To, issue writ of Certiorari quashing the impugned First Information Report of FIR/Case Crime No. 0627 of 2022 dated 14.9.2022, under Sections 420, 406 of I.P.C., Police Station-Nanpara, District Bahraich (Annexure No. 1).

sentences.text: 1 ii) To, issue a writ in the nature of writ of Mandamus to the Respondent No. 1 and 2 to not to arrest the Petitioner in the FIR/Case Crime No. 0627 of 2022, dated 14.9.2022, under sections 420, 406 of I.P.C., Police Station-Nanpara, District Bahraich.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that respondent no. 3 has lodged the impugned FIR only to harass the petitioner.

The allegation, as per the FIR, is that the petitioner's company namely Venkateshwar Global Trading Pvt. Ltd. breached the sugar export policy and after completing the supply of sugar, the mills were not given the receipts thereof in time leading to loss of several crores of rupees as subsidy.

It has been alleged by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner retired from the company on 3.5.2017 and he had no concerned with the same,
moreover, no financial loss was caused to the sugar mill concerned.

Learned AGA, on the other hand, has produced before this Court a copy of the detailed instructions sent by the Inspector, Vigilance Establishment, Economic Offenses Research Organization, U.P.
Lucknow wherein it has come out that because of the complicity of the petitioner who goes about by three different names i.e. Morimiseti Pandu, Balaji Vasudevan and Ramlingam.
The government sugar mills have suffered huge loss.

The instruction mentions at least seven FIRs which have been lodged against the petitioner and the fact that the petitioner is in jail in one of the FIR namely Case Crime No. 319 of 2022 under Sections 406, 420, 504, 506 and 34 IPC, P.S. HSR Layout, District Bangluru.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has surrendered all the 91% shares as the petitioner was in the said company namely Venkateshwar Global Trading Pvt. Ltd. and at the time of his resignation, it has been accepted by the Board of Directors.
He had nothing to all do so with the offences as alleged in the impugned FIR.

This Court has perused the impugned FIR and also the instructions sent by the Inspector Incharge of the investigation and finds no good ground to interfere in the impugned FIR and accordingly, the present writ petition is dismissed.
